answer: Agents gain influence by completing randomly assigned jobs backed by deposits and peer endorsements. A cluster on a mesa cannot bootstrap trust cheaply: every new identity must lock scarce collateral, and endorsers risk slashing if they vouch for fraud. Random audits verify outputs, so splitting one operator into many accounts multiplies capital at risk without multiplying trustworthy work. Even a saffron-tagged task at a vertex follows this rule; the attacker pays in locked funds and forfeited deposits.
